summary: Multi-account social UI iteration validated end-to-end. Backend: 16/16 multi-account pytest cases passed (GET /api/social/{platform}/accounts shape for all 3 platforms, 404 on unknown platform, 401 without X-User-Id, DELETE bogus id returns 502 without crashing the server, link-account set/clear/null/empty-string/404/400, link visible in /api/companies, social/connect returns redirect_url or already_connected). Scheduler verified via curl: scheduled_for in the past → status transitioned scheduled → failed within 60s, with a clean error in results[0] ('No connected account found for user ID … for toolkit linkedin'); the scheduler did NOT crash. Frontend: signed up a fresh random user, navigated to Settings, scrolled to the new 'Social accounts' section — LinkedIn/Facebook/Instagram each render with their colored icon, label, 'No accounts connected yet' subtitle, and a '+ Connect' button using the correct testIDs (settings-linkedin-connect, settings-facebook-connect, settings-instagram-connect). All buttons are visually enabled. Tapping +Connect for LinkedIn did NOT crash (WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync attempt under headless is a no-op). Legacy settings-{platform}-disconnect testIDs are correctly absent. No React render errors, no invalid keys, no missing imports. Only console noise is 4 × 401 from pre-mount unauthenticated profile/daily-prompt fetches (carried over from iteration 1, cosmetic).

minor.issue: When Composio returns 'Multiple connected accounts found' even with allow_multiple=True (some auth configs), the endpoint correctly falls through to {already_connected:true}. Acceptable, but the response loses the redirect_url so the UI can't initiate a fresh OAuth from a multi-account state. Consider explicitly calling client.connected_accounts.link(... allow_multiple=True) without the try/except fallback if the SDK supports it natively.

issues: The '+ Connect' button text concatenates the Ionicons glyph with 'Connect' as a single Text node (renders as `\uf103Connect`). It looks fine visually because the icon is wrapped in its own Ionicons component, but the plain-text DOM read returns the glyph + label without a space — only matters for screen readers / e2e text assertions. Cosmetic.

react_native_issues.component: expo packages version mismatch (carried over from iteration 1)
react_native_issues.issue: expo@54.0.34 (expected ~54.0.35), expo-font@14.0.11 (expected ~14.0.12), expo-router@6.0.23 (expected ~6.0.24). Logged at Expo CLI startup. Non-blocking; run `npx expo install --check`.

Helper text says 'tap + Add to save as a new company' which is misleading when no chips are shown — consider reworking the helper copy or always rendering the + Add chip.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/server.py:1205 — `info = await asyncio.to_thread(_info) if False else await asyncio.to_thread(_info)` is an obvious dead-code ternary (`if False else`). Functionally equivalent to a single await but confusing; simplify to `info = await asyncio.to_thread(_info)`.

/app/backend/server.py:1239-1253 — link-account uses empty $set when account_id is None (Mongo will error on `update_one({}, {'$set': {}, '$unset': {...}})` only if BOTH are empty). Current code is safe because $unset is always populated when $set is empty and vice versa, but worth a comment.

/app/backend/server.py:1098-1139 — _execute_social_post only supports LinkedIn (falls through with 'posting not yet supported' for facebook/instagram). The scheduler can therefore never successfully post a Facebook or Instagram scheduled post even if connected. Document or guard at POST /api/scheduled.
/app/frontend/app/(tabs)/settings.tsx — dead `disconnectSocial` helper still imports nothing dangerous but adds confusion; safe to delete.

rca_of_issue: Initial scheduler pytest reported a requests.ConnectionError 'Remote end closed connection without response' after ~50s of polling. Root cause: an idle keep-alive connection to localhost:8001 was dropped by the FastAPI/uvicorn worker mid-poll, not a backend bug. Reproduced the same scenario via plain curl (POST /api/scheduled, then sleep 80, then GET /api/scheduled) and the doc transitioned scheduled → failed with results[0].error containing the expected Composio 'No connected account found' message. Mitigation in the test would be to use a fresh requests.Session per poll or add a retry-on-ConnectionError; not changing because the underlying behaviour is correct.
